readings.text: A10.14 step 4 and 6, "refuses uncommitted changes": git status --porcelain --no-renames (untracked files listed one by one; a rename or copy counts both its paths) over the system folder and the reference folders of Hyperbolic Oracles and Engram Mind's Eye, whole (lexicon puts both on sys.path ahead of the standard library and imports hpstep and engram from them in place), must be empty, except the step's own outputs (so that an interrupted run resumes at the same HEAD); a sys.path entry inside the repository outside these folders is refused too. The check, with HEAD unchanged, is repeated before each worker pool starts (spawn workers import the code from disk afresh) and before the step writes its record; each check is listed (git_checks). "The only paths changed since the commit tuning ran on" (step 6) is git diff --name-only --no-renames, so a moved file names its old path too. --allow-dirty is refused in registered mode; in a dry run it marks the record "development run: not a registered run".

A10.14 "it resumes ... from its finished jobs": a runs.jsonl line is reused only at the same HEAD and configuration (mode, instance, epochs, burn-in, budget), and only while its cached float table, snapped text and per-query APs still have their recorded SHA-256s; anything else is rerun. A line trained under another environment is reused all the same ("that is the same run"): A10.4 has each run record its environment, so every job record carries the one its worker ran under (environment_sha, with the environments in run_environments), every start carries its own, and a reuse across environments is logged and counted (environments_summary).

A10.11 "wall-clock per run ... with the number of concurrent processes": time.perf_counter and time.process_time of the training, with the size of the pool that ran it (min(--workers, the jobs it ran): the most worker processes that run at once).

A10.4 "each run records the numpy, numba and libc versions and numpy's SIMD features": each job record holds the environment of the worker that ran it (Python, numpy, numba, llvmlite, libc, platform, numpy's CPU features and dispatch targets, the CPU model), computed inside the worker; the outputs give each run its environment_sha and list the environments once (run_environments).

A10.1 and A10.14, the replay check: the designated run's draws (tuning: (lorentz, 3, 0.03, first tuning seed); measure: measured (lorentz, 3, first training seed)) are replayed for every epoch of the budget with hpstep.prng.Rng, and the state after the run's last epoch (the epoch it diverged at, if it did) must equal its final state. If the designated cell is not run (no frozen lr, or the self-test's cells), the first run of the step in job order is replayed instead.

A10.8: tuning computes the exact snapped closure MAP of each finite table and nothing else (no graph-edge MAP, no float64 ranking); its per-query closure APs, float table, snapped text and epoch losses stay in the cache. tuning.json keeps the mean losses of epochs 0, 19, 99, 499 and 999.
